However, the neural networks (NNs) required by these applications often exceed the memory and energy budgets of wearable nodes. primary.title: DPS: Dual-Mode Precision LLM Serving with Semi-Unified Memory
primary.snippet: Existing LLM serving systems virtualize and optimize KV-cache memory, but treat model-weight memory as fixed throughout execution. Recent work on multi-precision model representations challenges this design by allowing a single stored model to support both full-accuracy and lower-precision execution, making the effective weight footprint runtime-dependent. science.title: ‘Vacuumtronics’ could help make better superconductors
science.snippet: Vacuum fluctuations can enhance superconductivity in a bulk material. This is the new finding from researchers in China and the US who have put forward the concept of “vacuumtronics”. This is a new way to tune superconductivity without chemically altering a material, applying pressure to it or driving it with intense light. In quantum electrodynamics, a vacuum is not empty but is host to fluctuating electromagnetic fields in which pairs of virtual particles are continuously being created and annihilated. Such vacuum fluctuations are thought to be responsible for phenomena like the Lamb shift , spontaneous emission and the Casimir effect . In recent years researchers have been looking into the possibility of exploiting these fluctuations to change the properties of bulk matter. science.title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.30249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2605.03922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive bounds on the lifetime of an evaporating black hole. The minimum lifetime bound follows from energy conservation and purification, within the framework of `asymptotically semiclassical spacetimes'. The recently derived expression for the Bondi flux of Hawking radiation, together with the expression for the entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation at null infinity, is used to investigate the purification phase after the last semiclassical ray. We discuss the energy-cost of entanglement purification and find a lower bound on the purification time of the black hole, which scales as $M_0^4/\hbar^{3/2}$, where $M_0$ is the initial black hole mass. reserve.title: Unification of Gravity and Standard Model: Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2508.10959v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a unified (quantum) description, by the gauge principle, of gravity and Standard Model (SM), that generalises the Dirac-Born-Infeld action to the SM and Weyl geometry, hereafter called Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). The theory is formulated in $d =4-2\epsilon$ dimensions. The WDBI action is a general gauge theory of SM and Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincar\'e symmetry), in the Weyl gauge covariant (metric!) formulation of Weyl geometry. The theory is SM and Weyl gauge invariant in $d=4-2\epsilon$ dimensions and there is no Weyl anomaly.
